messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED - dedicated-europe pool is at 98% GPU utilization and autoscaler failed to add capacity. Paginated on-call. thread_ts=1785554321

jen: I’m looking at the console - autoscale logs show repeated failures to launch instances: 
```
ERROR: failed to allocate node: insufficient quota in eu-west-1
Reason: quotaExceeded
```

jen: lots of 429s coming through for several customers, p95 latency spiking to 2.1s for text-gen, error rate ~6% last 5m

sahil: Confirming AcmeCorp and BrightHealth are seeing 429s and timeouts. Support reported multiple alerts.

lucas: On it — checking Dedicated pool config. We have burst disabled for that pool (policy: strict). I can flip to allow burst while we sort quotas.

maya: Recommending two-step mitigation: 1) temporary customer-level rate-limits for noisy customers 2) enable burst capacity on dedicated-europe and increase autoscaler burst size.

devon: +1. Also suggest redirecting lower-priority embedding jobs to hosted fallback pool to free GPUs.

jen: Can we do (1) quickly? Which customers should we throttle?

sahil: Throttle by route: /v1/generate.low-priority to 30r/s per-customer; keep high-priority SLAs (Auth-tier) as-is. Start with AcmeCorp and BrightHealth to 50% of their current traffic.

lucas: Applying rate limit now: `redwoodctl traffic limiter set --pool dedicated-europe --route /v1/generate.low-priority --limit 30r/s --customers AcmeCorp,BrightHealth`

ops-bot: Command queued: redwoodctl job id 8f3a. Will run in ~10s.

ops-bot: Job 8f3a succeeded. Rate limits active for AcmeCorp,BrightHealth on /v1/generate.low-priority

jen: App metrics show immediate drop in request volume to pool. Error rate for text-gen starts to fall (from 6% -> 3% in 2m).

lucas: Enabling burst capacity on dedicated-europe now. Command: 
```
redwoodctl pools update --pool dedicated-europe --burst-enabled true --burst-size 40
```

ops-bot: Requested pool update job 8f3b started.

ops-bot: Job 8f3b completed: burst-enabled=true, burst-size=40

maya: Autoscaler is now able to bring up surge nodes, provisioning 6 additional GPUs (estimated ready in ~90s).

devon: While that boots, I'll reroute non-sensitive embedding jobs to hosted to keep memory usage low. Running: `redwoodctl route set --src dedicated-europe --dest hosted-fallback --tags embeddings --threshold 0.7`

ops-bot: Route update job 8f3c completed. Non-critical embedding traffic redirected.

sahil: Customer impact update: AcmeCorp shows 429s reduced to single digits, latency p95 down to 1.1s. BrightHealth similar. No new customer escalations.

jen: Leaving a note for post-incident: need to request quota increase for eu-west-1, and revisit burst policy defaults for Dedicated pools.

lucas: I’ll open a ticket with cloud quota team and request a soft quota bump + schedule a follow-up to allow pre-provisioning for expected spikes.

maya: Also recommend we add an automated fallback route that moves non-SLA traffic to hosted-fallback when pool utilization > 85% for >1m. Could be a simple policy rule.

devon: Agreed. Will prototype a routing rule in staging.

ops-bot: Metrics stabilizing. Pool utilization dropping to 72% after new nodes came online and routing changes. Error rate at 0.9%.

sahil: On-call handoff in 20m — I’ll start the writeup. Devon, taking the next 2h of watch to ensure ramp-down is healthy.

devon: Taking over. If anything spikes back, call me or page eng-oncall.

jen: Thanks team. Postmortem owners: jen (incident lead), lucas (infrastructure), maya (routing/traffic policies).

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: sahil -> devon at 1785555400

sahil: Final note: temporary customer quota increases will be rolled back after 24h unless request approved. Documenting all commands run in incident ticket INC-2026-045.

jen: Closing thread for real-time ops. Will keep monitoring and post timeline in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
